newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian blue chips close higher, hotels down.
newsitem.headline: Croatian blue chips close higher, hotels down.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Wednesday with gains among the blue chips and losses among the hoteliers, and traders say this trend is likely to continue.
"Zagrebacka Banka, Pliva and Podravka will continue to gain gradually, while tourist firms will continue losing," a Ratko Zadravec of private brokers Zadravec said.
Of 14 active issues, nine rose, four were down and one remained flat. Volume was higher at 16,958, turnover lower at 10.6 million kuna.
Fully listed drug firm Pliva gained 101 kuna to close at 12,801 kuna on volume of 165 shares.

Other Croatian company listed on the London Stock Exchange, Zagrebacka Banka, gained 15 kuna to close at the all time high of 1,025, selling 4,122 shares. The bank's E-series shares were the biggest gainers, jumping more than 10 percent to close at 400 kuna.
Podravka food processor closed at 285, five up on the day's highest volume of 6,146 shares.
Among the biggest losers were three of the five Istrian hoteliers which scored spectacular gains in the past six weeks.
Jadranturist lost 52 kuna, closing at 360, Riviera fell 45 kuna to close at 250, both on meagre double-figure volumes. Arenaturist lost 35 kuna, closing at 245, with 338 shares sold.
Only Laguna gained 20 kuna to close at 1,560, as brokers say there is steady interest for it, and Istraturist remained flat at 340 on high volume of 3,298 shares.
Brokers predict that the hoteliers' prices were too high and are likely to fall back to about a double of their August starting positions.
Among the gainers was also cable producer Elka, rising 30 kuna to close at 300.
The central bank exchange rate was set at 5.4684 kuna for the dollar, up from 5.4458.
